experiments.why: Collinear run where the single top-level segment finds no deviation and must drop every interior vertex.
One segment whose only interior vertex is within tolerance, so the stack loop must not keep it.
One segment whose interior vertex exceeds tolerance and is kept with no further sub-segments to push.
Small wiggles all under tolerance, checking the iterative step collapses the run to its endpoints.
A tolerance whose square overflows to Infinity, standing in for Infinity, so nothing exceeds it.
Splits at several depths on both the left and right sides, so LIFO processing must keep exactly the same vertices as left-first recursion.
Two interior vertices tie for the maximum deviation, so the split must still pick the first one.
A near-monotonic convex edge that splits near one end at each level, leaving many segments pending on the explicit stack.
A closed ring whose first chord is degenerate, simplified at the zoom-0 degree tolerance, must come back closed.
A ring in Mercator meters with the mercatorToleranceForZoom(10) override, keeping a 10 m bump and dropping a 2 m one.
A small closed triangle at zoom 0 that runs the degenerate-chord split and must not throw.
An open line at the zoom-0 tolerance mixing dropped wiggles and kept corners across several split levels.

obligations.statement: simplify([[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[3,3],[4,4]], 0.001) drops every interior collinear vertex and returns exactly [[0,0],[4,4]].

source.quote: exact 3-vertex ring: middle vertex within tolerance is dropped

obligations.statement: simplify([[0,0],[0.5,0.001],[1,0]], 1) drops the middle vertex, whose deviation is within the tolerance, and returns [[0,0],[1,0]].
simplify([[0,0],[1,1],[2,0]], 0.001) keeps all 3 vertices because the middle vertex deviates by more than the tolerance.
simplify([[0,0],[1,0.1],[2,0],[3,0.05],[4,0]], 0.2) returns fewer than 5 points, starting with [0,0] and ending with [4,0].

source.quote: isLocked on specific vertex preserves it

obligations.statement: On the collinear ring [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[3,3],[4,4]] at tolerance 0.001, an isLocked predicate that locks the vertex with x === 2 makes simplify return 3 points with [2,2] kept between the two endpoints.
When isLocked returns true for every coordinate, simplify removes nothing: [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]] at tolerance 10 comes back with all 4 vertices.

source.quote: high-detail curve collapses under high tolerance

obligations.statement: A 101-point unit circle ([cos t, sin t] for t = i/100 * 2*pi, i = 0..100) simplified with tolerance 10 collapses to at most 5 points.

source.quote: @returns Simplified coordinate array (always preserves first and last point)

obligations.statement: For any input ring and tolerance, the array simplify returns begins with the input's first point and ends with the input's last point.
simplify returns inputs of one or two points unchanged: simplify([[0,0],[1,1]], 1) equals [[0,0],[1,1]] and simplify([[0,0]], 1) equals [[0,0]].
With tolerance 0, simplify keeps every vertex: simplify([[0,0],[0.1,0.1],[1,1]], 0) returns 3 points.
simplify([[0,0],[0.5,0.5],[1,1]], Infinity) returns only the 2 endpoints.

source.quote: huge ring 10k pts processed without crash + result <= input

obligations.statement: simplify on a 10,000-point ring of random points in [0,100) x [0,100) at tolerance 0.5 completes without throwing.

source.quote: simplifyPolygon at very low zoom (z=0) high tolerance

obligations.statement: simplifyLine([], 5) and simplifyLine([[0,0]], 5) do not throw.

source.quote: Preserves ring closure and minimum vertex count.

obligations.statement: For a closed input ring, every ring simplifyPolygon returns is still closed, with its last vertex equal to its first.
toleranceForZoom(z) returns 360 / (8192 * 2^z) degrees: about 360/8192 at z=0, 360/16384 at z=1 and 360/(8192*1024) at z=10, halving with each zoom level.
